title: KV shadowing and interactive burst budget: adaptive headroom for continuous batching
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Summary:
We need a pragmatic headroom and eviction strategy that optimizes inference cost and latency for interactive flows while maintaining SLOs under bursty traffic. This ticket introduces the KV shadowing pattern plus an adaptive burst budget that: (1) reserves a percentile-based KV/activation headroom for interactive tenants, (2) maintains a lightweight shadow store for recently-evicted KV prefixes to allow low-cost rehydration, and (3) coordinates with continuous batching to avoid eviction storms that spike tail latency.

Goals:
- Reduce tail token-latency regressions caused by large-tenant bursts and KV churn.
- Keep steady-state GPU memory utilization high for cost efficiency, but maintain predictable short-term headroom for interactive SLOs.
- Provide an explainable budgeting model (weights / KV / activations) used by admission control and the scheduler.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Percentile Headroom Ledger: compute per-tenant and per-pool headroom targets using 95th/99th token-length and interarrival percentiles from the last 7 days. Headroom expressed as three buckets: weight-resident reserve (static), kv-cache reserve (dynamic), and activation surge buffer (elastic).
2) KV Shadowing: when a KV prefix is evicted due to memory pressure, asynchronously copy a very small metadata snapshot (signature + compressed 256B LRU bloom) into host-side shadow store. If the prefix is requested within a configurable window (shadow_ttl), use shadow metadata to prefetch compressed deltas or rehydrate via prioritized background transfer to GPU before scheduling the request into a latency-sensitive lane.
3) Burst Budget Controller: each GPU pool maintains a token-burst budget that can be spent by interactive requests. The budget decays on a fixed cadence and is replenished based on steady-state free-memory and recent SLA compliance. Requests that would breach the budget are routed to a lower-cost lane or a quantized model fallback.
4) Continuous Batching Integration: the batcher will expose a KV-affinity hint API (hot/maybe/cold) so continuous-batching can prefer grouping hot-KV requests together and avoid packing cold-prefetch work into fast lanes.

Telemetry & Metrics (must have):
- kv_shadow_evictions_total, kv_shadow_rehydrate_hits, kv_shadow_rehydrate_misses, kv_shadow_prefetch_latency_p50/p95/p99
- burst_budget_spent_ratio, burst_budget_replenish_rate, requests_routed_to_fallback
- per-tenant memory breakdown: weights_bytes, kv_bytes, activations_bytes, headroom_reserved_bytes
- tail token latency by lane (fast/slow/fallback) and by kv-affinity

Implementation plan (tasks):
- infra: implement host-side shadow store with compact index and network-backed replication (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521)
- runtime: expose kv-affinity hint on Request proto and batcher changes to honor affinity grouping (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/batcher/pull/1187)
- scheduler: add burst budget ledger and admission check point in route planner (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/3033)
- eviction logic: add shadowing hook during kv eviction and rehydrate path with prioritized DMA pipeline (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4539)
- tests: unit + integration harness on local sim cluster to validate headroom replenishment and eviction-rehydrate paths (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/KV+Shadowing+Design)

Progress updates / timeline:
- 2026-02-18 (Ava): RFC shared on Confluence and design review scheduled. Collected initial latency incident traces for two customers showing kv-churn tail spikes.
- 2026-02-22 (Ravi): Prototype for shadow store on host implemented; baseline rehydrate POC shows median rehydrate 35ms, p99 210ms. Link: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521 (WIP).
- 2026-02-28 (SDET - Maya): Began integration test harness to simulate eviction storms and continuous-batching behavior with synthetic tenants. Early results: simple eviction+rehydrate without budgeting still causes p99 to climb beyond SLO during sustained bursts.
- 2026-03-03 (Ravi): Implemented a first-pass burst budget ledger and admission gate; added metrics emitted to telemetry. Staging run with blue/green variants shows 30% p99 improvement for interactive lane at 10% cost increase.
- 2026-03-10 (Team): Design review completed; action items: tighten shadow_ttl tuning, add tenant-pricing-informed budget caps, and run 72h stress test across mixed-model workloads.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end path for shadow eviction -> rehydrate is instrumented and p95 rehydrate <120ms in staging for 90% of rehydrates.
- Burst budget prevents any single tenant from causing >25% increase in pool-wide p99 token latency over baseline.
- Telemetry dashboards available in Console for per-tenant headroom accounting and burst budget consumption.
- Controlled rollout plan (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on latency SLO breaches.

Rollout plan:
- Canary (5%) on a single region with non-critical tenants; monitor rehydrate hit rate and p99 token latency for 72h.
- Expand to 25% with extended workloads and tenant sampling.
- Full roll (100%) after two successful canaries and runbook sign-off.

Runbooks and fallbacks:
- If burst_budget_spent_ratio > 0.9 for >10m and p99(latency) worsens, auto-throttle interactive lane and fall back to quantized-model route.
- If kv_shadow_rehydrate_miss ratio > 0.3, disable shadow-prefetch and revert to previous eviction policy while we investigate.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Shadow_ttl sizing: long TTL reduces rehydrate misses but increases host storage and consistency concerns. Propose default 2m, tune per pool.
- Prefetch cost vs lane contamination: background rehydrate can harm other requests if not rate-limited. We need a throttled DMA pipeline with QoS.
- Billing/observability: do we surface burst budget consumption in customer billing or keep it internal? Recommendation: internal first, expose as opt-in metric for enterprise tenants.

Next steps (short):
- 2026-03-11..2026-03-15: complete integration tests and 72h stress run across mixed-length token distributions.
- 2026-03-16: iterate shadow_ttl and prefetch QoS based on stress run.
- 2026-03-18: begin 5% canary rollout and monitoring playbook execution.

Notes on uniqueness: this ticket intentionally introduces the "shadowing" concept (compact host-side metadata to allow prioritized rehydration) and couples it with a replenishing burst budget rather than purely static reservations. The combination aims to provide both cost efficiency and predictable interactive latency under continuous batching workload patterns.
